to dive deep into some of the most common song structure sections Verse Chorus and Bridge let's start with the verse the verse is usually one of the first sections you hear in the song because of the first section they usually set the vibe for the song as well another notable aspect of verses is that they repeat themselves not in lyrics that's important or even instrumentation all the time but most of the time in melodic structure and chords the second verse copies a lot of ideas from the first and it makes it seem familiar to The Listener let's take a look at Gloria Gaynor's classic I Will Survive to find out more about the verses let's hop to the second verse keep in mind the melody that Gloria was singing and also keep in mind the chord structure underneath here we go very similar to the first verse but a lot more energetic this is reminiscent of that first verse just slightly different and notice the lyrics have changed too that's enough about verses let's hop into the chorus the chorus is the prom king of song sections they're the most popular the most talked about and probably the most important the chorus is almost always the catchiest part of the song and the part of the song that gets stuck in your head it's the part of the song that's singable and memorable and maybe one of the biggest reasons why you love a song the chorus often repeats itself and is an idea that shows up again and again in the same exact way sometimes choruses will differentiate themselves by adding more instrumentation more percussion or other elements like that but the lyrics themselves stay the same the melody stays the same and the chord structure says the same too let's take a look at a famous chorus from the Beatles Let It Be words of wisdom let it be let it be let it be let it be let it be whisper words of wisdom Let It Be I can hear you singing it now pretty catchy right courses don't have to be complex for them to be memorable but they should be one of the most enticing Parts about your song I often say to my students that the verse should be setting the storyline of what the feeling will be and then the chorus will be the general feeling that somebody has encapsulated in words if you're interested in learning more about song lyrics actually have a full guide on my website you can check that out in the description below now that takes us to the black sheep of the song section family the bridge the bridge is the most often overlooked of song structures the bridge serves as a musical breakpoint between the song often times after listening to the same part of a song for two three four minutes The Listener needs a break something that's in the same key something that feels like the rest of the song but changes it up enough to keep them interested without the bridge The Listener would just get bored let's take a look at a bridge that is an all-time classic from the song hey Ya by Outkast [Music] okay that would be an example of changing up the rhythm of the song it's changing up the rhythm of the lyrics changing up the melody and it keeps you interested especially when a bridge is as catchy as this now that I've defined what a verse A Chorus and a bridge are let me talk about the ways that people commonly mess up with song structure the first reason would be not understanding what song structure is this is the most prominent mistake I hear in songs that the song has a bunch of really cool melodic ideas but there's no obvious chorus in the song it's not a good thing when a minute and a half into the song and you haven't changed any of the chord structure any of the melodic structure either it gets boring keeping in mind basic sound structure as you write is usually enough to avoid this problem if you think about the song structure as you write if you have a guide then you're not going to fall into the Trap of creating something that is super confusing the next most common song structure mistake I hear is changing the sounds of each section beginners change the sound of each section so much that they lose cohesiveness song sections Define themselves by how they sound but they also Define themselves by the similarity to the other parts of sections with the same name for example verse 1 should be similar to verse 2. the first chorus should be similar to the second chorus keep them similar people it's what people have been listening to for years it's the formula that so many hit songs have followed and you should follow it too it's what listeners expect so give it to them the next mistake I see with song structure is changing the length of each section too much beginners make the mistake of making some sections really long and some sections really short compared to the rest of the song instead of changing the melody or the chords too much the first verse and the second verse are different only because the second verse is four times longer than the first verse I've heard songs with the first chorus being 16 Bar the second chorus being 64 bars and then the last chorus being eight bars that is a big change it's not uncommon for you to have your last course be twice as long but it shouldn't be five times longer than your verse now it's time to talk about exactly what good song structure looks like and I'm also going to give you some examples of songs that use that song structure I think the best way for you to understand good song structure is to study some of the most popular songs out there and analyze the structure that they have now if that sounds like a lot of
